# NexRoute 0.6.4 — hardening, evidence and explainable ranking

NexRoute 0.6.4 is a hardening release for the 0.6.x line. It keeps the 0.6.3 Discord/YouTube strategy refresh and focuses on making the evidence, ranking, updater and release supply chain easier to verify and harder to misinterpret.

## Strategy Lab

- Replaces the legacy one-shot synthetic score with repeated observations.
- Prioritises critical-service availability above secondary checks.
- Adds stability as a first-class signal so flapping 1-of-3 / 2-of-3 results are visible instead of looking equivalent to stable behavior.
- Treats the GitHub control endpoint as an eligibility gate rather than score input.
- Marks insufficient or ambiguous runs as `inconclusive` with a null score instead of manufacturing a zero.
- Excludes missing optional latency/loss/jitter/throughput measurements and renormalises the remaining score weights.
- Stores endpoint and protocol pass rates, observation counts, control results and a deterministic winner explanation.
- Preserves readability of legacy Strategy Lab history.
- Native Dashboard displays the same ranking state, critical availability, stability, observation count and winner explanation used by the CLI.

## Privacy-safe field evidence

- Adds deterministic Strategy Lab field-evidence receipts tied to both the candidate SHA-256 and source-log SHA-256.
- Requires one strategy to pass the complete critical Discord/YouTube target set and healthy Google/Cloudflare controls.
- Rejects unknown targets, unknown statuses, incomplete target sets, split success across multiple strategies and modified receipts.
- Canonical receipts contain no provider, location, username, SSID, MAC address, absolute local path or wall-clock verification time.
- Raw Strategy Lab logs are not part of the publication receipt.
- A privacy-review mode describes excluded categories before publication.

## Updater transaction hardening

- Adds a post-update health check inside the existing backup/restore transaction.
- Verifies the installed version, required runtime files and the 23-target patch report before the transaction is considered healthy.
- When NexRoute was running before the update, the Windows runtime must return to a healthy running state.
- A deterministic test hook forces post-update health failure so rollback can be exercised in CI.
- CI includes a Windows migration evidence gate using the real published 0.6.2 and 0.6.3 archives, including a path with spaces and Cyrillic, state preservation, second-run idempotence and forced-health rollback.

## GitHub Actions supply-chain hardening

- Every external action in every current and legacy workflow is pinned to a reviewed full 40-character commit SHA.
- Human-readable semantic-version comments remain next to the executable pins.
- Repository validation rejects mutable refs, unknown actions, unreviewed SHAs and mismatched version comments.
- The reviewed update procedure is documented in `docs/GITHUB_ACTIONS_PINNING.md`.

## Release trust flow

The 0.6.4 release workflow continues to produce and verify:

- `NexRoute-0.6.4-win-x64.zip`
- `NexRoute-0.6.4-win-x64.zip.sha256`
- `NexRoute-0.6.4-validation.json`
- `NexRoute-0.6.4-validation.md`

The release workflow verifies the pinned upstream archive, builds and tests the package, proves an offline rebuild, verifies native controllers and launchers, and generates GitHub build provenance for the published subjects.

## Compatibility

- Windows x64 remains the packaged target.
- Existing 0.6.x user state remains part of the updater preservation contract.
- 0.6.4 does not introduce the planned 0.7.0 strategy-manifest redesign.

See `docs/RELEASE_0.6.4_ACCEPTANCE.md` for the automated and manual acceptance gates used before final publication.
